title: Boundary Handling
text: Standard LOWESS neighbourhoods become asymmetric boundaries: fewer points exist one side, pulling local fit toward data interior. boundary_policy parameter controls data padded mitigate effect.

title: Boundary Handling
text: Pads beyond endpoints replicating first last observed values. Prevents fit curling toward zero. Use : strong prior boundary behaviour; general-purpose smoothing.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(boundary_policy = "extend") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (extend policy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (extend policy): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4862648 0.4942855 0.5026953 0.5114688 0.5205144 0.5296957

title: LOWESS Concepts
text: LOWESS (Locally Weighted Scatterplot Smoothing) nonparametric regression method fits smooth curves scatter plots without assuming global functional form. Unlike parametric methods (linear regression, polynomial fitting), LOWESS adapts locally data structure, making ideal : Exploratory data analysis — Discover patterns without assumptions Trend estimation — Extract signals noisy time series Baseline correction — Remove systematic effects spectroscopy Genomic smoothing — Smooth methylation, ChIP-seq, expression data

title: LOWESS Concepts
text: point data, LOWESS: Selects neighbors — Choose nearest points (controlled fraction) Assigns weights — Closer points get higher weights (using kernel function) Fits locally — Perform weighted least squares regression Extracts value — Use fitted value smoothed estimate Iterates (optional) — Reweight points based residuals reduce outlier influence

title: LOWESS Concepts
text: fraction (also called bandwidth span) important parameter. controls proportion data used local fit. Tip: Start fraction=0.67 (default) adjust based visual inspection. Use cross-validation automated selection.

title: Custom Weights
text: Per-observation weights encode data quality directly LOWESS fit. Standard LOWESS assigns equal prior trust observations. Custom weights let override assumption point point — distance robustness weighting applied. effective weight observation jj local fit centred xix_i : wij=custom_weights[j]×K(dijhi)×rjw_{ij} = \text{custom\_weights}[j] \times K\!\left(\frac{d_{ij}}{h_i}\right) \times r_j KK distance kernel, hih_i local bandwidth, rjr_j robustness weight current iteration. Note: custom_weights applies Batch mode . silently ignored Streaming Online adapters.

title: Custom Weights
text: compose: use simultaneously. Custom weights suppress known bad points; robustness iterations handle residual outliers.

title: Custom Weights
text: Set weight 0 bad point — excluded every local fit.
code: library(rfastlowess)  x <- 1:10 y <- x * 2.0 y[6] <- 100.0              # spike at index 6  weights <- rep(1.0, 10) weights[6] <- 0.0          # exclude the spike  model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.5, iterations = 0L) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights) cat("First 6 smoothed values (outlier excluded, no robustness):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (outlier excluded, no robustness): print(head(result$y)) #> [1]  2.572621  4.000000  6.000000  8.000000 10.000000 12.000000

title: Custom Weights
text: Weight 1/σi21/\sigma_i^2 measurement uncertainties known.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.5)  # Measurement precision varies along x sigma <- 0.1 + 0.5 * abs(sin(x)) weights <- 1 / sigma^2  model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.3) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights)  plot(x, y, pch = 16, cex = 0.5 + weights / max(weights),     col = "gray", main = "Inverse-Variance Weighted LOWESS") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

title: GPU Backend
text: batch Lowess type can execute GPU-accelerated backend powered wgpu (Vulkan / Metal / DX12). GPU backend reimplements almost entire LOWESS pipeline — local regression fitting, robustness iterations, interval bounds, cross-validation — compute shaders, anchor points fitted parallel. Batch . GPU support applies batch Lowess type . StreamingLowess OnlineLowess remain CPU-. GPU acceleration worth enabling roughly 10K+ points. smaller inputs CPU backend (optionally parallel = TRUE) typically faster GPU dispatch overhead accounted .

title: Confidence and Prediction Intervals
text: Estimate uncertainty smoothed curve .
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.5, confidence_intervals = 0.95) result <- fit(model, x, y)  # Plot with bands plot(x, y, pch = 16, col = "gray",     main = "LOWESS with 95% Confidence Intervals") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_lower, col = "blue", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_upper, col = "blue", lty = 2)

title: Confidence and Prediction Intervals
text: Wider confidence intervals — cover new observations fall.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.5, prediction_intervals = 0.95) result <- fit(model, x, y)  plot(x, y, pch = 16, col = "gray",     main = "LOWESS with 95% Prediction Intervals") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$prediction_lower, col = "red", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$prediction_upper, col = "red", lty = 2)

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Kernel functions determine neighbouring points contribute local fit. Points closer target receive higher weights.

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Efficiency = AMISE relative Epanechnikov (1.0 = optimal)

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Cleveland’s original choice. Best -around performance. w(u)=(1−|u|3)3w(u) = (1 - |u|^3)^3 Use : Default choice applications.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(weight_function = "tricube") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (tricube kernel):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (tricube kernel): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4862648 0.4942855 0.5026953 0.5114688 0.5205144 0.5296957

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Optimal AMISE sense. Slightly angular tricube. w(u)=34(1−u2)w(u) = \frac{3}{4}(1 - u^2) Use : Statistical optimality matters; compact support desired.
code: model <- Lowess(weight_function = "epanechnikov") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (epanechnikov kernel):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (epanechnikov kernel): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4980927 0.5058916 0.5141306 0.5214559 0.5283514 0.5346370

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Unbounded support — points non-zero weight. w(u)=e−u2/2w(u) = e^{-u^2/2} Use : Smooth transitions boundaries; periodic data.
code: model <- Lowess(weight_function = "gaussian") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (gaussian kernel):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (gaussian kernel): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.5254291 0.5307319 0.5394626 0.5378479 0.5402746 0.5415505

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: smooth, compact support. w(u)=(1−u2)2w(u) = (1 - u^2)^2 Use : Extra smoothness required; robust heavy tails.

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Smooth, cosine-shaped weight. Efficient compact. w(u)=π4cos⁡(πu2)w(u) = \frac{\pi}{4}\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi u}{2}\right) Use : Smooth result compact support; slightly faster biweight.

title: Merge Strategies
text: Streaming LOWESS processes data fixed-size chunks configurable overlap. Points inside overlap zone fitted twice — left chunk right chunk. merge_strategy decides two estimates combined.
code: Chunk A:   [=========|=====] Chunk B:            [=====|=========] Overlap:            [=====]                       ↑                  merge_strategy                  applied here

title: Merge Strategies
text: Blends left- right-chunk estimates using distance-based weights. Points closer centre chunk get higher weight. Use : General-purpose streaming; reliable option.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3) x_chunk <- x[seq_len(50)] y_chunk <- y[seq_len(50)]  model <- StreamingLowess(     merge_strategy = "weighted_average",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (weighted_average strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (weighted_average strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Merge Strategies
text: Takes arithmetic mean left-chunk right-chunk estimates overlap region. Use : Chunks large overlap region uniform data density.
code: model <- StreamingLowess(     merge_strategy = "average",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (average strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (average strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Merge Strategies
text: Uses left-chunk estimate overlap region. Use : left chunk larger context window expected accurate overlap boundary.
code: model <- StreamingLowess(     merge_strategy = "take_first",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (take_first strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (take_first strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Merge Strategies
text: Uses right-chunk estimate overlap region. Use : right chunk expected provide better context (e.g., data follows).
code: model <- StreamingLowess(     merge_strategy = "take_last",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (take_last strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (take_last strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Quick Start
text: LOWESS can robustly handle outliers iterative reweighting:
code: library(rfastlowess)  x_out <- seq(1, 6, length.out = 6) y_with_outlier <- c(2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 50.0, 10.0, 12.0)  model <- Lowess(     fraction = 0.5,     iterations = 5,     robustness_method = "bisquare",     return_robustness_weights = TRUE ) result <- fit(model, x_out, y_with_outlier)  for (i in seq_along(result$robustness_weights)) {     if (result$robustness_weights[i] < 0.5)         cat(sprintf("Point %d is likely an outlier (weight: %.3f)\n",                     i, result$robustness_weights[i])) }

title: Robustness
text: Standard LOWESS can biased outliers. Robustness iterations downweight points large residuals: Fit initial LOWESS Compute residuals Assign robustness weights (large residuals → low weight) Refit using combined distance × robustness weights Repeat steps 2–4

title: Robustness
text: Smooth downweighting. Points transition gradually full weight zero. w(u)={(1−u2)2|u|<10|u|≥1w(u) = \begin{cases} (1 - u^2)^2 & |u| < 1 \\ 0 & |u| \geq 1 \end{cases} Use : General purpose, balanced approach.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "bisquare") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (bisquare robustness):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (bisquare robustness): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4862648 0.4942855 0.5026953 0.5114688 0.5205144 0.5296957

title: Robustness

title: Scaling Methods
text: iterations > 0, LOWESS computes robustness weights comparing residual current residual scale estimate. scaling_method parameter controls scale measured. robustness weight point ii : wi=B(|ri|6⋅σ̂)w_i = B\!\left(\frac{|r_i|}{6 \cdot \hat{\sigma}}\right) BB bisquare function σ̂\hat{\sigma} scale estimate. larger σ̂\hat{\sigma} makes algorithm tolerant large residuals; smaller one makes aggressive.

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=median(|ri−median(ri)|)\hat{\sigma} = \text{median}(|r_i - \text{median}(r_i)|) First centers residuals median, takes median absolute deviations. Double use median makes highly resistant extreme outliers. Use : Data may contain outliers (default applications).
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mad") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (MAD scaling):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (MAD scaling): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4862648 0.4942855 0.5026953 0.5114688 0.5205144 0.5296957

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=median(|ri|)\hat{\sigma} = \text{median}(|r_i|) Slightly less robust MAD center residuals first, faster compute. Use : Residuals roughly symmetric around zero; speed concern.
code: model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mar") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (MAR scaling):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (MAR scaling): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4870733 0.4951594 0.5036339 0.5124703 0.5215762 0.5308144

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=1n∑|ri|\hat{\sigma} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i |r_i| Least robust — influenced outliers. Matches classic OLS residual scale. Use : outliers expected; comparisons classical methods.
code: model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mean") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (mean scaling):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (mean scaling): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.5023604 0.5119281 0.5219198 0.5323007 0.5429772 0.5538188

title: Use Case: Genomic Data Smoothing
text: LOWESS well-suited genomic data DNA methylation profiles, ChIP-seq signals, expression arrays. Sequencing depth variation, PCR artifacts, biological heterogeneity create noise LOWESS handles gracefully without parametric assumptions.

title: Use Case: Genomic Data Smoothing
text: small fraction = 0.1 lets LOWESS follow fine-scale spatial structure without smearing transitions methylated unmethylated regions. confidence_intervals = 0.95 produces uncertainty bands naturally widen positions sparser CpG coverage.
code: library(rfastlowess)  # Simulate methylation data along a chromosome set.seed(42) n <- 1000 positions <- sort(runif(n, 0, 1e6))  # True methylation pattern true_meth <- 0.5 + 0.3 * sin(positions / 1e5)  # Observed with noise observed <- true_meth + rnorm(n, sd = 0.15) observed <- pmax(0, pmin(1, observed))  # Smooth model <- Lowess(     fraction = 0.1,     iterations = 3,     confidence_intervals = 0.95 ) result <- fit(model, positions, observed)  # Plot plot(positions, observed, pch = ".", col = "gray",     xlab = "Genomic Position (bp)", ylab = "Methylation Level",     main = "Methylation Profile Smoothing") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_lower, col = "blue", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_upper, col = "blue", lty = 2) legend("topright", c("Observed", "Smoothed", "95% CI"),         pch = c(1, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, 2),         col = c("gray", "blue", "blue"))

title: Use Case: Genomic Data Smoothing
text: ChIP-seq experiments produce sparse, noisy coverage data. LOWESS can help identify binding regions. fraction = 0.05 provides high spatial resolution — important resolving narrow binding peaks otherwise smeared background. larger iterations = 5 deliberate: Poisson-distributed read counts produce tall, isolated spikes, extra robustness iterations progressively -weight estimated background level inflated handful extreme counts.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42)  # Simulated ChIP-seq enrichment n <- 500 positions <- seq(1, 50000, length.out = n) signal <- 10 + 5 * dnorm(positions, mean = 25000, sd = 5000) * 1000  # Add noise and spikes noise <- rpois(n, lambda = 2) signal_noisy <- signal + noise signal_noisy[c(100, 200, 300)] <- signal_noisy[c(100, 200, 300)] * 5  # Smooth model <- Lowess(     fraction = 0.05,     iterations = 5 ) threshold <- quantile(result$y, 0.75)  plot(positions, signal_noisy, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = "gray",     xlab = "Genomic Position", ylab = "Read Count",     main = "ChIP-seq Signal Smoothing") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) abline(h = threshold, col = "red", lty = 2)

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
text: data arrives continuously sensors, logs, streaming pipelines, Online adapter provides incremental smoothing without reprocessing entire dataset.

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
text: window_capacity = 25 limits internal buffer 25 recent observations; add_point() call costs O(window) rather growing total history. min_points = 5 suppresses output window holds enough points stable fit. update_mode = "incremental" re-fits recent point rather full window, halving typical latency.

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
code: library(rfastlowess)  set.seed(42) times <- 1:100 temperatures <- 20 + 5 * sin(times / 10) + rnorm(100)  model <- OnlineLowess(     fraction = 0.3,     window_capacity = 25,     min_points = 5,     update_mode = "incremental" ) for (i in seq_along(times)) {     result <- add_point(model, times[i], temperatures[i])     if (!is.null(result))         cat(sprintf("Time %d: %.2f\n", times[i], result$y))     if (i >= 10) break  # print only the first few outputs } #> Time 5: 22.80 #> Time 6: 22.72 #> Time 7: 24.73 #> Time 8: 23.49 #> Time 9: 25.94 #> Time 10: 24.14

text: LOWESS provides flexible trend extraction time series without parametric assumptions. handles irregular sampling, noise, outliers naturally.

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: fraction = 0.1 sizes neighbourhood 10% data evaluation point — narrow enough follow slowly varying trend without smearing periodic variation. Three robustness iterations -weight noise spikes.
code: library(rfastlowess)  set.seed(42) t <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 500) trend <- 10 + 0.5 * t + 3 * sin(t / 10) noise <- rnorm(500, sd = 3) y <- trend + noise  model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.1, iterations = 3) result <- fit(model, t, y)  plot(t, y, col = "gray", pch = ".",     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Value", main = "Trend Extraction") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("Observed", "Trend (LOWESS)"),         pch = c(1, NA), lty = c(NA, 1), col = c("gray", "blue"))

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Extract trend component compute residual inspect seasonality.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42)  # Simulate monthly data with trend + seasonality + noise t <- 1:120  # 10 years monthly trend <- 100 + 0.5 * t seasonal <- 15 * sin(2 * pi * t / 12) noise <- rnorm(120, sd = 5) y <- trend + seasonal + noise  # Extract trend with large fraction (heavy smoothing) model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.4, iterations = 2) result <- fit(model, t, y)  # Residual = observed - trend (should show seasonality) residual <- y - result$y  par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 0.5)) plot(t, y, type = "l", col = "gray",     main = "Original + LOWESS Trend", xlab = "Month", ylab = "Value") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)  plot(t, residual, type = "l", col = "darkgreen",     main = "Detrended Residual (Seasonal Component)",     xlab = "Month", ylab = "Residual") abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "red") par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: LOWESS handles irregularly sampled data naturally — interpolation needed.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42)  # Irregular sampling: dense early, sparse later t_irregular <- c(sort(runif(200, 0, 50)), sort(runif(50, 50, 100))) y_irregular <- sin(t_irregular / 10) + rnorm(length(t_irregular), sd = 0.5)  model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.2, iterations = 2) result <- fit(model, t_irregular, y_irregular)  plot(t_irregular, y_irregular, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = "gray",     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Value", main = "Irregularly Sampled Time Series") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Prediction intervals widen uncertainty band include uncertainty fitted curve expected scatter new observations. fraction = 0.2 offers balance local detail stable interval width.
